positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS TO EXPAND THE FINBIN DATABASE TO INCLUDE UNIFORM DATA FROM WESTERN BEEF COW-CALF AND BACKGROUNDING OPERATIONS, SUPPORT IMPROVED RANCH MANAGEMENT KNOWLEDGE, AND ADVANCE RANCHER RISK MANAGEMENT DECISION-MAKING. WHILE THE FBMB DATABASE REPRESENTS 11 STATES AND MORE THAN 2,300 FARMS AND RANCHES, THERE IS A LACK OF REPRESENTATION FROM BEEF COW-CALF AND BACKGROUNDING ENTERPRISES (143 AND 12, RESPECTIVELY) AND WESTERN RANCHES. COLORADO IS A LEADER IN BEEF PRODUCTION AND ITS UNIQUE REGIONAL LANDSCAPES WOULD INCREASE THE DIVERSITY OF BEEF ENTERPRISES IN THE DATABASE AND EXPAND THE IMPACT OF FINBIN TO THE WESTERN UNITED STATES. THIS PROJECT WILL MAKE BENCHMARKING DATA RELEVANT TO WESTERN BEEF CATTLE PRODUCERS, ULTIMATELY IMPROVING THEIR PROFITABILITY, COMPETITIVENESS, AND ABILITY TO SUCCESSFULLY MANAGE THROUGH PERIODS OF HIGH RISK, VOLATILITY, AND FINANCIAL STRESS.THE GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO 1) ENHANCE WESTERN BEEF PRODUCERS' RANCH FINANCIAL LITERACY AND RECORD KEEPING SKILLS; 2) IMPROVE BEEF PRODUCERS ABILITY TO SUCCESSFULLY MANAGE THOUGH PERIODS OF HIGH STRESS; AND 3) MAINTAIN AND EXPAND BEEF PRODUCER RELATIONSHIPS TO FURTHER ENHANCE THE FBMB AND COLORADO SPA DATABASES.TO ADDRESS THESE GOALS, WE WILL MEET THE FOLLOWING PROJECT OBJECTIVES: 1) DEVELOP A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO OBTAIN FINPACK AND CO SPA LEVEL DATA FROM BEEF PRODUCERS IN COLORADO AND CREATE A LONG-TERM PERFORMANCE-TRACKING DATABASE; 2) CREATE RISK MANAGEMENT TOOLS TO FACILITATE PRODUCER AND STUDENT LEARNING AND IDENTIFY RANCH FINANCIAL STRESS PRECURSORS; AND 3) LEVERAGE EXISTING EXTENSION PROGRAM STRUCTURE TO EXPAND DATABASES AND DELIVER BENCHMARKING RESULTS. UPON CONCLUSION OF THIS PROJECT, WE ANTICIPATE WESTERN BEEF PRODUCERS WILL HAVE A GREATER UNDERSTANDING OF FACTORS THAT AFFECT OPERATIONAL PROFITABILITY AND WILL UTILIZE THE KNOWLEDGE GAINED TO MAKE MORE INFORMED MANAGEMENT DECISIONS. WE HOPE TO DEVELOP A COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARKING TRAINING PROGRAM THAT INTEGRATES INTO OUR EXISTING EXTENSION STRUCTURE AND ALLOWS FBMB AND SPA PARTICIPANTS TO SUSTAINABLY MANAGE THEIR BEEF ENTERPRISES. DURING THE PROJECT PERIOD, WE EXPECT (60) RANCHERS TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE AND (30) OF THOSE SAME RANCHERS TO CONTRIBUTE TO COLORADO SPA. SPECIFICALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL AIM TO INCREASE IN BEEF PRODUCER FINANCIAL LITERACY AND RECORD KEEPING SKILLS, IMPROVE OVERALL MANAGEMENT AND PROFITABILITY OF WESTERN BEEF COW-CALF OPERATIONS, INCREASE THE NUMBER OF TRAINED RANCH MANAGEMENT ADVISORS ASSISTING PRODUCERS AT THE LOCAL LEVEL, AND GENERATE SIGNIFICANT DATA FOR RESEARCH AND GRADUATE STUDENT TRAINING. WE ARE COMMITTED TO UTILIZING THE RESOURCES DEVELOPED IN THE EXECUTION OF THIS PROJECT TO CONDUCT FUTURE TRAINING AND ENSURE THE SUSTAINABILITY OF RANCH ENTERPRISES AND FULFILL GOALS OF THE FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT & BENCHMARKING PROGRAM.?

positiveFlows.title: THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO BROADEN THE COLLECTION OF FARM LEVEL FINANCIAL AND PRODUCTION DATA TO ASSIST IN THE DEARTH OF INFORMATION PRESENTLY AVAILABLE IN THE STATE OF SOUTH CAROLINA. THIS PROJECT WILL NOT ONLY ASSIST IN INCREASING THE NATIONAL DATABASE BUT THROUGH THIS PROCESS BUT WILL ADVANCE THE TEAMS DATA GATHERING AND RESEARCH CAPABILITIES ON COST OF PRODUCTION, DEVELOP A BASE FOR CASES TO TEST AGRICULTURAL AND FARM POLICY AND TO BE USED IN THE TEACHING OF FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT COURSES, PROVIDE MORE PRECISE INFORMATION FOR EXTENSION OUTREACH EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING INITIATIVES, AND IMPROVE THE FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS OF SOUTH CAROLINA AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS.THE CLEMSON UNIVERSITY EXTENSION AGRIBUSINESS TEAM WILL LEVERAGE ITS STAFF AND SOUTH CAROLINA AGRIBUSINESS PARTNERS TO COLLECT THE NECESSARY INFORMATION FROM 15 FARMS ADDING 15 ADDITIONAL FARMS EACH YEAR OF THE THREE-YEAR PROJECT TO PERFORM AN ACCRUAL FARM ENTERPRISE FINANCIAL ANALYSIS. DATA WILL BE COLLECTED THROUGH ONE-ON-ONE CONSULTATIONS AND THROUGH OTHER EXTERNAL SOURCES THAT PROVIDE LENDING AND ACCOUNTING RESOURCES TO FARMERS. ALL PARTICIPATING FARM INFORMATION WILL BE AGGREGATED AS IT IS ENTERED INTO THE CENTER FOR FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENTS FINBIN SYSTEM.

WE WILL BUILD FROM OUR TWO-YEAR PILOT BENCHMARKING GRANT WITH THE CENTER FOR FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND ADD 35 PRODUCE AND/OR MAPLE OPERATIONS TO THE NATIONAL DATABASE.PRODUCERS INTEGRATING COST-BASED PRICING DECISIONS TO DETERMINE THE PRODUCTS THAT FIT THEIR SPECIFIC MARKETS, MARKETS THAT FIT THEIR FARMS, AND IDENTIFYING PRODUCTS THAT FIT THEIR FARM'S SYSTEMS. THE DEVELOPMENT OF EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH MATERIALS THAT CAN BE UTILIZED ACROSS STATES AND VIA ON-LINE PLATFORMS SUCH AS EXTENSION.THE ESTABLISHMENT OF AN ASSOCIATION OF PRODUCERS AND EDUCATORS TO SHARE EXPERIENCES AND IDEAS ABOUT HOW TO OPERATIONALIZE FINBIN OUTPUT AND IMPROVE PROFITABILITY, EFFICIENCY, AND OTHER RELATED FARM CHALLENGES.

positiveFlows.title: THE INTENT OF THIS PROJECT IS TO USE A 5-STATE COLLABORATION TO PROVIDE TRAINING FOR NEW FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS AND TO EXPAND THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE. THIS WILL IMPROVE FARMER'S LIVES BY IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF THEIR FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS, AND BY PROVIDING ADDITIONAL DATA FOR AN INDIVIDUAL FARMER TO BENCHMARK AGAINST. 175 FARMS WILL BE ADDED TO THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE. THE COLLABORATION IN THIS PROJECT WILL ENSURE THAT BOTH TRADITIONAL FARMERS AND SPECIALTY CROP PRODUCERS ARE ADDED TO THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE. IN DOING SO, THIS PROJECT WILL ADDRESS MEASURES 2 AND 4 OF THE FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT AND BENCHMARKING COMPETITIVE GRANTS PROGRAM.TRAINING AND MENTORING WILL BE DELIVERED AT NORTH CAROLINA A&T WHERE NEW PROGRAMS ARE BEING DEVELOPED AND IN WISCONSIN AS IT MANAGES STAFF CHANGES IN NUMEROUS EXISTING PROGRAMS. THIS PROJECT WILL, IN A NEW WAY, ADDRESS MEASURE 3 OF THE FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT AND BENCHMARKING COMPETITIVE GRANTS PROGRAM.THIRDLY, A NEW SIMPLIFIED PRODUCER TOOL WILL BE DEVELOPED TO PROVIDE PRODUCERS WITH AN ENHANCED UNDERSTANDING OF INFORMATION PROVIDED BY THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE. THIS TOOL WILL BE SHARED WITH PARTICIPATING FARMERS TO LIMIT THE FEELING OF BEING OVERWHELMED BY DATA, ENABLE THEM TO BETTER EXAMINE THE FINANCIAL CONDITION OF THEIR FARM, AND DISCOVER THEIR BEST FINANCIAL PATH FORWARD FOR THEIR FARM. THIS INITIATIVE WILL ADDRESS MEASURE 5 OF THE FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT AND BENCHMARKING COMPETITIVE GRANTS PROGRAM.IN GENERAL, FARMERS IN NORTH CAROLINA AND WISCONSIN WILL HAVE BETTER PREPARED FARM MANAGEMENT PROFESSIONALS ASSISTING THEM AS THEY EVALUATE THE FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF THEIR FARM BECAUSE MENTORING SUPPORT WILL COME FROM ILLINOIS, MINNESOTA, AND MISSOURI. ILLINOIS, MINNESOTA, AND MISSOURI WILL ADD NEW FARMS TO THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE ALLOWING THEIR FARMERS TO BENCHMARK THEIR FARMS TO AN EXPANDED DATABASE.

positiveFlows.title: THIS PROJECT WILL ACHIEVE THREE SETS OF GOALS. FIRST, THE PROJECT WILL MAINTAIN AND EXPAND THE NATIONAL FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT DATABASE (FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE) BY CONTRIBUTING A VARIETY OF IDAHO CROP AND LIVESTOCK BUDGET DATA FROM THE LONG-STANDING UNIVERSITY OF IDAHO (UI) CROP AND LIVESTOCK BUDGETING AND BENCHMARKING (IDAHO-AGBIZ) PROGRAM. SECOND, IT WILL IMPROVE THE AWARENESS AND USE OF THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE AMONG IDAHO'S DIVERSE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS WHO ARE INVOLVED IN THE PRODUCTION OF 185 COMMODITIES ON ALMOST 25,000 FARMS. THIRD, THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH AN INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAM ON THE OPTIMAL RISK MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES, ESPECIALLY FOR SMALL- AND MEDIUM-SIZED FARMS USING THE FBMB NATIONAL DATABASE. SPECIFICALLY, THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE REPRESENTATIVE AND DETAILED FINANCIAL INFORMATION, COVERING A BROAD NUMBER OF PACIFIC NORTHWEST AND INTERMOUNTAIN FARM SECTORS TO UPDATE AND AUGMENT THE PUBLICLY AVAILABLE FARM FINANCIAL DATABASE. THE PROJECTWILL SUPPORT AND STRENGTHEN FARM MANAGEMENT DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES BY INCREASING ACCESS TO FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT INFORMATION FROM COMPARABLE OPERATIONS. THE PROJECT WILL BE CONDUCTED BY UI EXTENSION FACULTY WHO HAVE NUMEROUS YEARS OF EXPERIENCE IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND DELIVERY OF REPRESENTATIVE FARM FINANCIAL AND ENTERPRISE ANALYSIS.

positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** DEMANDS FOR LOCAL BEEF HAVE CONTINUALLY INCREASED OVERTIME BUT EXPLODED DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. AS MORE DIRECT TRANSACTIONS OCCUR AMONG PRODUCERS, PROCESSORS, AND CUSTOMERS OF LOCAL BEEF, CHALLENGES SURFACED DUE TO UNCERTAINTIES AND LACK OF COMMUNICATION AMONG STAKEHOLDERS REGARDING TRANSACTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, OUR PRELIMINARY SURVEY SHOWED THESE B2C BEEF PRODUCERS DO NOT FULLY UTILIZE STANDARDIZED FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT TECHNIQUES FOR MAXIMIZING PROFITABILITY POTENTIAL. TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES, THIS MULTI-DISCIPLINARY PROJECT AIMS TO MAXIMIZE PROFITABILITY POTENTIAL OF SMALL- AND MEDIUM-SIZED B2C BEEF PRODUCERS BY DEVELOPING RESOURCES RELATED TO FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT/COST CONTROLS, BENCHMARKING, AND LOCAL BEEF PURCHASING. DEVELOPED RESOURCES WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AT 18-24 RANCHES IN KANSAS, AND THEIR FINANCIAL INFORMATION WILL BE ADDED TO THE NATIONAL FARM FINANCIAL DATABASE (FINBIN).DELIVERABLES INCLUDE (1) BENCHMARKING DATA OF 18-24 BEEF PRODUCERS IN KANSAS AND (2) RESOURCES FOR PRODUCERS, PROCESSORS, AND CUSTOMERS OF LOCAL BEEF: FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT/COST CONTROL AND LOCAL BEEF PURCHASING. AN AGRICULTURAL ECONOMIST WILL VISIT BEEF PRODUCERS 2-3 TIMES, YEARLY, TO COLLECT OPERATIONAL/FINANCIAL DATA TO EXPAND FINBIN AND TO PROVIDE CONSULTATIONS USING THE DEVELOPED RESOURCES. CHANGES IN FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE AND SATISFACTION WITH B2C TRANSACTIONS WILL BE USED TO ASSESS THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE DELIVERABLES. THE PROJECT WILL CULMINATE IN A FREE ONLINE RESOURCE REPOSITORY.

positiveFlows.title: THIS PROJECT WILL MAINTAIN AND EXPAND THE EXISTING FINBIN FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT DATABASE, WITH A FOCUS ON FACILITATING COLLABORATION FROM MORE DIVERSE FARM MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES, EXPANDING RESEARCH OPPORTUNITIES, AND EXPANDING THE TYPES OF FARMING ACTIVITIES REPRESENTED IN THE DATABASE. positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** THE CENTER FOR FARM FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT (CFFM) WILL MAINTAIN AND EXPAND THE EXISTING NATIONAL FARM FINANCIAL DATABASE, FINBIN, WITH A FOCUS ON EXPANDING COLLABORATIONS TO HELP PRODUCERS ANSWER IMPORTANT FINANCIAL AND ECONOMIC QUESTIONS RELATING TO TOPICS SUCH AS CONSERVATION PRACTICES, DIRECT MARKETING, AND AQUACULTURE. THIS PROJECT WILL CONTINUE TO WORK TO REMOVE GEOGRAPHICAL BARRIERS FROM FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT EDUCATION BY CONTINUING TO PILOT THE VIRTUAL FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT PROGRAM WITH THE FARMER VETERAN COALITION IN VARIOUS REGIONS OF THE COUNTRY. THIS PROJECT WILL ALSO COLLABORATE WITH PARTNERS TO EXPAND THE EMERGING AQUACULTURE BENCHMARKING PROJECT AND OTHER EMERGING PROGRAMS ACROSS THE COUNTRY. CFFM WILL WORK WITH COLLABORATORS TO INCREASE THE AMOUNT OF DIRECT MARKETING AND VALUE-ADDED ENTERPRISES SUBMITTED TO THE NATIONAL DATABASE, MAKING IT MORE REPRESENTATIVE OF THE ENTIRE SPECTRUM OF U.S. AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS. TO ENHANCE THE EFFICIENCY OF FINANCIAL ANALYSIS FROM CONTRIBUTING PROGRAMS, THIS PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE USE OF A CLOUD-BASED VERSION OF FINPACK (FINPACK+) FOR FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT EDUCATORS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS PROJECT WILL DEVELOP THE ABILITY IN THE NATIONAL DATABASE TO BENCHMARK FIELDS USING COVER CROPPING PRACTICES OVER MULTIPLE YEARS TO BETTER ASSESS ANY POTENTIAL IMPACTS OF THOSE PRACTICES.

THE NEW WEB APPLICATION WILL PROVIDE PRODUCERS WITH A REPORT CARD TO BENCHMARK THEIR OPERATIONS AGAINST OTHERS AND TRACK THEIR PROGRESS OVER TIME. TO MODERNIZE THE PROGRAM, THERE IS A PLAN TO CONVERT THE SPA FORMAT FROM EXCEL AND ACCESS TO A MORE USER-FRIENDLY WEB APPLICATION, BROADEN ITS SCOPE TO INCLUDE OTHER INDUSTRY SEGMENTS, AND UPDATE ALL CALCULATIONS TO ALIGN WITH CURRENT FARM FINANCIAL STANDARD COUNCIL GUIDELINES. THE NEW WEB APPLICATION WILL PROVIDE PRODUCERS WITH A REPORT CARD TO BENCHMARK THEIR OPERATIONS AGAINST OTHERS AND TRACK THEIR PROGRESS OVER TIME. WORKSHOPS WILL BE CONDUCTED ACROSS TEXAS TO PROMOTE THE NEW SPA WEB APPLICATION, AIMING TO ENGAGE AT LEAST 240 PRODUCERS OVER TWO YEARS AND ENCOURAGE MORE PRODUCERS TO GET INVOLVED. THE GOAL IS TO MAKE DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS MORE ACCESSIBLE AND USER-FRIENDLY, ULTIMATELY HELPING PRODUCERS IMPROVE THEIR EFFICIENCY, PROFITABILITY, AND OVERALL OPERATION.
positiveFlows.recipient: TEXAS A&M AGRILIFE EXTENSION SERVICE

positiveFlows.title: **AWARDS ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 20, 2025, WERE FUNDED UNDER PREVIOUS ADMINISTRATIONS AND MAY NOT REFLECT THE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES OF THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION.** WE PROPOSE A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS AND INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER EDUCATION TO IMPROVE THE KNOWLEDGE OF U.S. FARMERS AND RANCHERS. THE INTENTION OF OUR PROJECT IS TO IMPROVE LONG-TERM PROFITABILITY AND PRODUCER RISK MANAGEMENT DECISIONS THROUGH THE USE AND DEVELOPMENT OF THE NATIONAL FARM FINANCIAL BENCHMARKING DATABASE. THE PROJECT WILL BE CONDUCTED THROUGH THE EFFORTS OF THREE FARM BUSINESS MANAGEMENT ASSOCIATIONS IN NEBRASKA, SOUTH DAKOTA, AND NORTH DAKOTA, AND TWO LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES (OHIO STATE UNIVERSITY AND THE UNIVERSITY OF NEBRASKA-LINCOLN).OUR PROJECT WILL ADDRESS BOTH FBMB PROGRAM OBJECTIVES TO 1) MAINTAIN AND EXPAND THE NATIONAL DATABASE AND 2) EXPAND COLLABORATIVE FARM MANAGEMENT EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS AND ASSOCIATION PARTNERSHIPS THAT WILL CONTRIBUTE DATA TO THE NATIONAL DATABASE. WE WILL ALSO HELP TO ADDRESS ALL FIVE FBMB MEASURES IDENTIFIED IN THE FUNDING ANNOUNCEMENT. WHILE OUR ORGANIZATIONS ALREADY SUPPORT OVER 1,680 PRODUCER FARM FINANCIAL ANALYSES AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE NATIONAL DATABASE, WE ARE COMMITTED TO INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS (ESPECIALLY BEGINNING AND SMALL- AND MEDIUM-SIZED FARMS), INCREASING THE QUALITY OF FINANCIAL RECORDS, AND CREATING A COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL REPORT TO BE USED IN THE NATIONAL DATABASE. OUR PROJECT WILL ALSO SUPPORT RESEARCH RELATED TO IDENTIFYING THE INFLUENCE AND ROLE OF INFORMATIONAL AVOIDANCE IN FINANCIAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT DECISION MAKING. INSIGHTS WILL BE USED TO IMPROVE EXTENSION EFFORTS INFLUENCING BETTER FINANCIAL AND RISK MANAGEMENT DECISION MAKING. AMOUNT REQUESTED: $499,343.
positiveFlows.recipient: BOARD OF REGENTS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF NEBRASKA
